control_plane_follow_ups: Completing ADMIN-013 turns `npm run agents:validate` from 0 warnings / 0 errors to 0 warnings / 8 errors, and `--strict` reports the same 8. All eight are consequences of the completion transition, not of the code change, and all eight are dispatch decisions this task did not silently make. (1) Seven handoffs in docs/engineering/handoffs/pending/ are status 'accepted' with accepting_task_id ADMIN-013: HF-DB008-SCHEMA-MISSING-ADMIN, HF-DB008-TYPECHECK-ANALYTICS, HF-DB008-UNRESOLVED-ADMIN, HF-DB008-TYPECHECK-ADMIN, HF-DESIGN-031-ADMIN, HF-INTG-033-CODEQL-OAUTH-STATE-HASH, HF-INTG-033-MIGRATION-VALIDATION-HIRING-EXPIRY. The validator rejects an accepted handoff whose accepting task is completed (control-plane-validation.mjs:300), so each must be re-pointed to a live admin task or closed. They are the realignment tool's parked work, not part of AC-1, and their records are owned jointly with their sending lanes. Note HF-DB008-TYPECHECK-ADMIN lists this route in its working set, but its subject is the profiles.display_name / profiles.phone code-drift cluster; this change adds no profiles.* column access, so its substance is unaffected. (2) ADMIN-014 (docs/engineering/tasks/blocked/ADMIN-014.json) declares depends_on [ADMIN-013] with execution_state waiting_dependency, so it must now leave waiting_dependency for dispatch; its resume_condition 'All dependencies complete: ADMIN-013' is satisfied.

Remedy for the orchestrator: point the seven handoffs at a live admin task (or close the ones whose subject is already resolved), then activate ADMIN-014. Re-running `npm run agents:validate` afterwards should return to 0 errors.
